one_line: Royal patron from 13th-century Odisha who commissioned the Ananta Vasudeva Temple in Bhubaneswar.

appearance.age_look: Late 20s, graceful and poised, medium height with a dignified, slightly athletic build.
appearance.face: Heart-shaped face, medium-brown Odia complexion, straight nose, sharp yet kind almond eyes, a small beauty mark under the left eye, default expression calm and resolute with a gentle, knowing half-smile.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair parted slightly off-center, drawn back into a smooth, low bun at the nape and wrapped with a narrow gold cloth band; a simple gold maang-tikka at the parting and a small cluster of jasmine flowers pinned above the left ear.
appearance.costume: She wears a 13th-century Odia royal-style sari: a full-length handwoven deep maroon silk sari with a wide mustard-gold border featuring fine geometric Odishan temple motifs, draped in an early eastern style with the pleats in front and the pallu brought over the left shoulder to fall modestly down the back; beneath it a fitted short-sleeved choli in muted teal silk, fully covering the torso; a thin off-white cotton under-skirt visible only at the hem; jewellery is dignified and temple-appropriate—medium-sized gold hoop earrings, a layered gold necklace with small Vaishnava pendants, several slim gold bangles on both wrists, an ornate gold waist-belt (mekhala) cinching the sari at the hips with small hanging leaf-shaped charms, and a simple gold ring on her right hand; her feet are in brown leather mojari-style slippers with understated stitching; a finely woven light beige cotton shawl with a subtle red border is folded over her right forearm, ready to be drawn over her head when entering the temple.
appearance.signature: A rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin red cotton cord, held carefully in her left hand, representing the temple’s foundation charter and her patronage orders.

ref_desc: Chandrika Devi is a late-20s Odia royal woman with medium-brown skin, black hair in a low bun with gold band and jasmine, in a deep maroon sari with mustard-gold borders, teal choli, gold jewellery, brown slippers, and holding a red-tied palm-leaf manuscript.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model of Chandrika Devi from 13th-century Odisha: a late-twenties royal woman, medium-brown complexion, heart-shaped face, straight nose, almond eyes with a calm resolute half-smile, and a small beauty mark under her left eye. Her thick black hair is parted slightly off-center and drawn back into a smooth low bun at the nape, wrapped with a narrow gold cloth band, adorned with a simple gold maang-tikka and a small cluster of jasmine flowers above her left ear. She wears a historically grounded Odia royal sari: deep maroon silk with a wide mustard-gold border decorated in fine geometric temple-like motifs, draped with front pleats and the pallu passing over her left shoulder and falling modestly down her back; beneath it a fitted short-sleeved muted teal silk choli fully covering her torso and an off-white cotton under-skirt just peeking at the hem. Show her temple-appropriate jewellery: medium gold hoop earrings, layered gold necklace with small Vaishnava pendants, slim gold bangles on both wrists, an ornate gold mekhala waist-belt with tiny hanging leaf charms, and a simple gold ring on her right hand. On her feet are brown leather mojari-style slippers with subtle stitch patterns. A light beige cotton shawl with a narrow red border is folded neatly over her right forearm, and in her left hand she holds her signature prop, a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin red cotton cord, symbolizing the Ananta Vasudeva Temple’s foundation charter. Use deep maroon, mustard gold, muted teal, medium brown skin tone, and light beige as the dominant colours, and present her front, three-quarter, and back views to clearly display face, hair, garments, jewellery, and the manuscript.
